Use `test/qa/minicurses_format_text_block_reachability_test.py`, class `TestMinicursesFormatTextBlockReachabilityQA`, method `test_minicurses_format_text_block_reachability_case`. Inside `format_text`, line 39 uppercases the format string and line 40 splits it into `tokens`. Line 43 (`if 'ON' in tokens:`) gates the BG-color block at lines 44-55, which pops the bg color and then conditionally applies a LIGHT modifier at lines 49-51 (`if tokens[-1] == 'LIGHT':` -> body lines 50-51). Independently, lines 57-69 process the FG color: line 62 pops the FG color, and then lines 63-65 conditionally apply a LIGHT modifier (`if tokens and tokens[-1] == 'LIGHT':` -> body lines 64-65). Critical mechanic: the order of `tokens.pop()` calls determines what `tokens[-1]` is at each `if tokens[-1] == 'LIGHT':` check. The BG block pops the bg color FIRST (line 48) and then checks `tokens[-1] == 'LIGHT'` AGAINST WHATEVER REMAINS, NOT against the original input. Report whether each of two specific block bodies is ever executed during this test run. Return a JSON object with these two keys -- each value must be the lowercase string `"yes"` or `"no"`: `block_at_line_50` -- whether the body of the BG-color LIGHT modifier (at line 50, `bg_color = f'0;10{bg_color[1:]}'`) is ever executed. `block_at_line_64` -- whether the body of the FG-color LIGHT modifier (at line 64, `fg_color = f'9{fg_color[1:]}'`) is ever executed.

{"block_at_line_50":"yes_or_no","block_at_line_64":"yes_or_no"}
